    "file": "t54.js",

    "evidence": "res.on(\"data\", (chunk) => { body += chunk; });",
    "llm_reasoning": "In Node.js, strings are immutable. Using '+=' to concatenate chunks of data in a stream results in the creation of a new string object for every chunk received. For large responses, this leads to O(n^2) memory allocation behavior and excessive garbage collection pressure, as the engine must repeatedly copy the existing string content into a new, larger memory buffer.",
    "suggested_fix": "Collect chunks in an array and use Buffer.concat() or join them once at the end: \nconst chunks = [];\nres.on('data', (chunk) => chunks.push(chunk));\nres.on('end', () => resolve(JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString())));",

    ]
  }
